test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-3) Official Paper (Held On: 17 June 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following branches of language does NOT belong to the Indo-European family of languages?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Finno-Ugric.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A couple of dialects spoken on the European mainland are excluded from the** Indo-European group **of dialects.
 
• Finnish, Hungarian and Estonian have a place with the Uralic (likewise called Finno-Ugric) family, and Basque (expressed in the Pyrenees locale) has no hereditary connection to some other languages.
 
• The Finnic division of **Finno-Ugric** dialects is made out of five gatherings. The Baltic-Finnic bunch comprises **Finnish, Estonian, Karelian (counting Olonets), Ludic, Veps, Ingrian, Livonian, and Votic. **
 
• **The Permic bunch comprises Komi (Zyryan), Permyak, and Udmurt (Votyak).**
 
• The three most-communicated Uralic dialects, Hungarian, Finnish, and Estonian, are undeniably remembered for Finno-Ugric, albeit phonetic roots normal to the two parts of the customary **Finno-Ugric language tree (Finno-Permic and Ugric)** are far off.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other than Latin, the realized old Italic dialects are Faliscan (the nearest to Latin), **Umbrian and Oscan (or Osco-Umbrian), and South Picene.**
 
• The Indo-European family is partitioned into a few branches or sub-families, of which there are eight gatherings with dialects still alive today: **Albanian, Armenian, Balto-Slavic, Celtic, Germanic, Hellenic, Indo-Iranian, and Italic;** and another six regions that are currently terminated.
 
• Out of an all-out European populace of** 744 million starting around 2018, some 94%** are local speakers of an Indo-European language; inside Indo-European, the three biggest phyla are **Romance, Germanic, and Slavic with in excess of 200 million speakers each, between them, representing near 90% of Europeans.**
